newsitem.title: KENYA: Nairobi stocks ease, turnover doubles.
newsitem.headline: Nairobi stocks ease, turnover doubles.

text.p: The Nairobi Stock Exchange (NSE) 20-share index edged downwards on Tuesday although turnover more than doubled Monday's trading, bourse officials said.
The index lost 4.29 points to close at 3443.61. Turnover leapt to 40.8 million shillings traded on 618,532 shares, from 18.6 million traded on 618,843 on Monday.
"The market's been more or less cool on the main board. Only the bond market has been picking up over the last few days," said a trader.
Tuesday saw mixed fortunes in the agricultural sector, with heavy trading on thoroughbred Sasini Tea and Coffee, while Rea Vipingo Plantations shares took a dive.
"Turnover shot up because of a lot of shares in Sasini were bought," said a bourse official.
Brokers reported that a local buyer had bought 100,000 shares in the profitable exporter, while a foreign buyer snapped up 147,000 shares at 82.50 shillings.
"Sasini did very well, it's half year performance was very good. Shares have basically been scarce until today, when one person made them available," said a broker.
Rea Vipingo Plantations was Tuesday's loser, its tumble from 8.15 to 7.00 shillings was described by one trader as "disastrous."
Activity was sluggish in the Commercial and Service sector, with Kenya Airways unchanged on 8.0 shillings, and Uchumi Supermarket still pegged at 37.50.
Said by brokers to be traditionally a good performer, Kenya Commercial Bank gained 2 shillings to close at 105, while National Industrial Credit remained on 60, unchanged since Friday.

While the shares market remained slow, trading on treasury bills was brisk. The fourth issue of the Central Bank of Kenya floating-rate treasury bond traded 195.1 million shillings on 102.1817 percent from 101.89 percent.
One bourse offical said political uncertainty was making bonds more popular as they are perceived as safer investments.
"People are waiting to see what's happening," he said.
